purpose: Compare pretrained baseline vs conservative anti-forgetting checkpoint (step 25) vs degraded 500-step pilot on the matched 12-prompt validation set.

evidence: model.generate() has no internal EOS stop and always emits exactly max_new tokens; eos_count=0 for all 24 pretrained and fine-tuned generations

EOS_None (id 2), BOS_None and PAD_None all decode to silence (0 notes) in the tokenizer, but the fine-tuned model emits NO EOS tokens for the collapsed GMD prompts -- it simply predicts note-free sequences
GMD drum prompts collapse to 0-1 note after the 500-step fine-tune while validation loss improves (2.4509), a signature of catastrophic forgetting / overfitting on the small NRG-CP+GMD set

acceptance_gates.rule: All MIDI parse; <=1 of 6 prompts per source with <=1 note; mean notes per source >=70% of pretrained baseline; mean duration per source >=70% of pretrained baseline.

pretrained_vs_degraded_500step.assessment: degraded pilot collapsed generation, especially drums

pretrained_vs_step_25.assessment: step 25 preserves NRG-CP and substantially recovers GMD vs the degraded pilot; GMD duration modestly below pretrained but well above the 70% gate

checkpoints.note: Large checkpoint files are preserved locally and MUST NOT be committed to Git.

recommendation: The conservative step-25 update passes all generation-quality gates and recovers GMD drum generation without regressing NRG-CP. Continue to evaluate steps 50/75/100 against the same gates; if any gate is violated, preserve that checkpoint and stop. Do not extend training purely on validation loss. Any longer proposal must address catastrophic forgetting, per-source evaluation, rhythmic diversity, and broader electronic-genre data with authoritative labels.
